newsitem.title: CHINA: China newspaper says no deaths in Beijing blast.
newsitem.headline: China newspaper says no deaths in Beijing blast.

text.p: An explosion on a bus in the Chinese capital Beijing caused no deaths but injured more than 10 passengers, the official Beijing Daily said on Saturday.
Chinese sources said a bomb on the public bus in the western Xidan district killed at least two people and injured around 30 on Friday.
The Beijing Daily report was the first official confirmation of the blast.
"Yesterday evening at about 7.00 p.m. (1100 GMT), an explosion occurred on a city Number 22 bus at the Xidan Market stop," the Beijing Daily said in a brief front-page report.
"More than 10 passengers were hurt, none was killed," the newspaper said, adding the incident was under investigation.
Workers at an emergency centre near the bustling commercial area told Reuters they had sent about 30 people injured in the blast to nearby hospitals for treatment.
One young man who said he saw the explosion blow the windows out of the back of the bus reported seeing about nine people seriously hurt.
A police official said that some people were suffering from burns but he declined to give further details.
The blast follows a string of bombings by Moslem separatists in the far western region of Xinjiang.

Three bombs planted on buses blew up within minutes of each other on February 25 in the region's capital of Urumqi in an attack apparently coordinated to coincide with funeral rites in Beijing for paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
